data.narrative:
Zap Energy, a Series D nuclear energy technology company founded by Benj Conway, Brian A. Nelson, and Uri Shumlak, operates within a sector represented by 3 public comparables (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 7 private peers including Helion, Oklo, and Valar Atomics. The company has raised $330M+ to date.

The valuation analysis employs stage-progression methodology, the sole applicable triangulation approach given insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage peer density in nuclear energy. Using total capital raised ($330M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.5x step-up multiplier typical for Series D advancement yields an implied valuation of $495M. A peer-median approach cannot be supported: while 6 same-sector companies exist, filtering for identical stage, adjacent stage, or comparable valuation tier produces fewer than the minimum 3 required datapoints, rendering sector-wide median comparison misleading.

Analysis supports a valuation range of $421M (low) to $569M (high), centered on $495M. Key uncertainties include the absence of narrow-set peer comparables—limiting confidence in stage-based multipliers—and structural differences within nuclear energy subsectors that may render even the identified peer set imperfectly comparable. The stage-progression method's reliance on a single multiplier introduces sensitivity; tighter calibration would require either closer-stage nuclear peer data or disclosed valuation terms from recent rounds.
